memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After a long time had passed and the Lord had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, Joshua, by then a very old man, summoned all Israel — their elders, leaders, judges and officials — and said to them: "I am very old." — Josh 23:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua is now a very old man. The battles are behind him, the land is at rest, and he knows his days are drawing to a close. So he gathers the leaders of Israel — elders, judges, officials — to speak to them one last time. And he begins with plain honesty: "I am very old."

There is something moving about a faithful servant at the end of his journey. Joshua does not pretend he will go on forever. He faces his own mortality openly and uses his remaining strength to point others to God. His final concern is not his own legacy but the faithfulness of the people after he is gone.

This teaches us to number our days wisely (Ps 90:12). None of us knows how long we have, and a life well lived keeps that truth in view — not with fear, but with purpose. Joshua's age did not make him useless; it made his words weighty. He had walked with God long enough to know what mattered most.

Whatever season you are in, ask what you would want to say if these were among your final words. What truth would you press upon those you love? Like Joshua, may we spend our days, especially our later ones, pointing others to the God who has been faithful to us all along.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live with an honest awareness of how brief life is?
2. What truths would you most want to pass on to those you love?
3. How are you using this season of life to point others to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to number my days and to use my life, in every season, to point others to You. Make my remaining years count for Your glory. Amen.
